html:
We can map distinct phenomenology to specific regimes of the loss landscape:

Boredom and Frustration: These states represent the vanishing of the intrinsic reward signal (rtint→0r_t^{\text{int}} \to 0), acting as "interrupts" that force policy exploration. Boredom occurs when model evidence is high and stable (the domain is fully compressed/mastered). Frustration occurs when model evidence remains low despite computational effort (the domain is irreducible noise or requires priors the agent does not yet possess). Frustration bifurcates into two computationally distinct cases: (i) stochastic frustration, where H(o|s)H(o|s) is genuinely high, signaling the agent should disengage; and (ii) structural frustration, where compression would be possible given appropriate priors, signaling the agent should backtrack to prerequisite subskills. Distinguishing these requires second-order inference about model class adequacy–a metacognitive capacity that itself develops. The relationships in this account are summarized schematically (Figure).

Flow and the Learning-Performance Paradox: The phenomenon of "Flow" 1 presents a theoretical tension: it is characterized by "effortless" action and high performance (suggesting a fixed, perfected model), yet it is driven by challenge and complexity (suggesting active learning). This is resolved by synthesizing Schmidhuber’s compression drive with Friston’s active inference 2. Schmidhuber’s principle provides the drive: the agent seeks high-complexity regimes to maximize compression velocity. Active inference provides the mechanism: to remain viable in these high-entropy regimes without experiencing "surprise" (a spike in free energy), the agent must adopt a state of maximal precision weighting on its current policy. In this state, counterfactual planning and self-referential monitoring are suppressed because the path of error minimization is unambiguous. Thus, Flow is not static perfection, but the phenomenological signature of "surfing the gradient"–deploying high-precision priors to successfully assimilate a complex, high-entropy data stream that is on the verge of becoming unmanageable. The hierarchical model makes the flow-state account explicit (Figure).

Aesthetics as Sudden Compression: Experiences of humor, insight, or aesthetic appreciation can be modeled as "structured violations"–inputs that initially spike prediction error but allow for a rapid, global re-encoding of the latent state. The resulting sudden drop in description length (a "Eureka" moment) generates a high-magnitude pulse of intrinsic reward. Formally, aesthetic pleasure can be modeled as rtint=Lt−ϵ−Ltr_t^{\mathrm{int}} = L_{t-\epsilon} - L_t where ϵ→0+\epsilon \to 0^+ but ΔL\Delta L is large–a high-bandwidth compression event. This explains why effective jokes require setup (establishing a high-entropy prior) followed by a punchline that retroactively compresses it, and why repeated exposure kills humor (the prior is no longer high-entropy).

This framework also reframes social learning (Vygotsky’s scaffolding) as cooperative loss-landscape smoothing. A teacher or caregiver acts as an auxiliary controller that actively reduces environmental variance, keeping the student within the high-gradient regime of learning and preventing them from falling into the local minima of boredom or the plateaus of frustration. More specifically, effective scaffolding can be understood as the teacher performing active inference on the student’s model, selecting demonstrations and hints that:

1. Lie within the student’s current zone of positive ΔL\Delta L (comprehensibility), 2. Maximize the student’s compression progress (informativeness), and 3. Sequence exposures to respect prerequisite structure (curriculum design).

Interestingly, this teacher-objective is itself a form of compression: the teacher seeks the minimal intervention sequence that induces maximal model improvement in the student. Language acquisition exemplifies this–caregiver speech ("motherese") is systematically simplified and structured to track the child’s current model capacity, a phenomenon termed "fine-tuning" by developmental linguists.
